LESSON: PRESERVATION OF CEREALS AND PULSES

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade five
Subject: General
Strand: Food Production Processes
Topic 2.3: Preservation of Cereals and Pulses
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Preservation of Cereals and Pulses, part of Food Production Processes in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade five General.

Key inquiry question: How does preservation and storage of cereals and pulses enhance food security?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Preservation of Cereals and Pulses together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
Unity: taking turns while undertaking tasks in preservation of cereals and pulses.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Food and nutrition security as learners preserve available cereals and pulses to prevent food wastage and spoilage.

Link to other subjects:

Learners relate skills in preservation of cereals and pulses to farming activities in the community learnt in Social Studies.
